hypotheses.note: IsCircuit ε x of the strict CycleGcd (the orbit reading, p ≥ εn − 1 as printed). The steps take an explicit run length q (the paper's p; in Lean p is p_n). The finiteness theorems take IsCircuit ε x; the proof's p ≥ εn implies p ≥ εn − 1, so they cover both readings.
Both. The 3-adic step, the identity and the bound hold for every q ≥ 1. noCircuit_l244_eps and the finiteness use q ≥ εn − 1, the weaker condition. noCircuit_l244_of_eta uses the proof's q ≥ εn.

n ≥ 2, with T^m x ≠ x for 0 < m < n. At n = 1 the step of l.227 is false (noCircuit_step_period_one_false, at (−1)). The circuits of least period 1 are the fixed points (1) and (−1), both known, so the statement is not affected; the proof as written does not exclude them.
i ∈ ℤ; the run is carried as printed.
One sequence α, n-periodic, with α k = a_k(x). A_u(y) is read as A_u(a(x)). The IsCircuit point y = T^m(x) gives the run at i = m (noCircuit_period_bounded_of).
Both readings: Aun (printed, 3^q) and AunAlt (3^{q−1}). The identity holds for both, with a factor 3 for AunAlt.

The bound of l.235 is proved without η (noCircuit_abs_diff_le). The η-forms (noCircuit_l235_of_eta, noCircuit_l244_of_eta) assume the partial-sum bound of the stray display l.253, 2^{a_{p+i+1}+⋯+a_{p+i+m}} ≤ (3+η)^m, as an explicit hypothesis. The draft does not prove it.

hypotheses.paper: Matveev's theorem (theo:matveev l.156–159; the display l.240)
hypotheses.note: Cited, so carried as an explicit hypothesis, never an axiom: NoCircuitMatveev C (the shape of theo:matveev, 3ⁿ < 2^P ⇒ 2^P − 3ⁿ ≥ 2^P/(eP)^C) or NoCircuitMatveevAbs C (l.240 as printed, with the absolute value and no sign condition). C is a parameter, with 0 ≤ C for the finiteness. This is T-syr-cited's question.
The true l.244 does not need it and holds on every cycle of ℤ (noCircuit_l244). Only the η-form, in the paper's shape, uses x > 0 (noCircuit_l244_of_eta).
Replaced by p_n ≤ 2n, proved on every cycle of ℤ (strict twoDesc_p_le). With the natural log the printed bound is false on every positive cycle (noCircuit_l243_natural_log_false).

A parameter K (NoCircuitStatement K, and the second conjunct of noCircuit_of_cited, for every K). The reading of the four known cycles of ℤ is noCircuitKnown. The reading 'the cycle (1, 4, 2) of the abstract' is refuted (noCircuitStatement_false_of_neg_one).

findings: syracuse.tex:221–247 — the proof does not reach the statement. It stops at l.244, an inequality that bounds n. Two things are missing: a bound of l.235 with η < ε, and a check of every smaller n. What the steps give in their true form is proved, with Matveev's theorem as a hypothesis. On every cycle of ℤ of least period n ≥ 2 with a run of q ≥ 1 ascending indices, 3^{q+1} 2ⁿ ≤ 2·3ⁿ (e p_n)^C (Syracuse.noCircuit_l244). That is 3^{n(ε − log₃(3/2))} ≤ 2(2en)^C for q ≥ εn − 1 (noCircuit_l244_eps). So for ε > log₃(3/2) ≈ 0.369, one B bounds the least period of every ε-circuit of ℤ (noCircuit_period_bounded; noCircuit_period_bounded_pos for x > 0 from theo:matveev's shape). The statement for that ε thus reduces to the ε-circuits of least period ≤ B. noCircuit_of_cited states this reduction with the bound as its first conjunct. Its earlier form, ∃ B, (check up to B) → statement, was a tautology, provable for every ε and K with no hypothesis; the audit caught it, and it is not to be reintroduced. For 10⁻¹⁴ ≤ ε ≤ log₃(3/2) the inequality holds for every n and bounds nothing (noCircuit_l244_eps_vacuous). The statement is recorded as the Prop NoCircuitStatement K and not proved.

syracuse.tex:222, 227 — the step needs n ≥ 2. « since i ≠ i+1 and n is a minimal period, A_{p+i} − A_{p+i+1} ≠ 0 » is false at n = 1, where i ≡ i + 1. The fixed point (−1) is an ε-circuit for every ε, has runs of every length, and A_{q+i} − A_{q+i+1} = 0 (noCircuit_step_period_one_false). For n ≥ 2 the step holds for both readings of OQ-43 (noCircuit_diff_ne_zero, from the strict Aun_sub_ne_zero_of_minimal).

syracuse.tex:227–229 — the step is true for the printed A_u^n. On a cycle of ℤ of least period n ≥ 2, with a_{i+k} = 1 on ⟦1, q⟧, 3^q (2^{p_n} − 3ⁿ) divides A_{q+i} − A_{q+i+1} ≠ 0. So 3^q |2^{p_n} − 3ⁿ| ≤ |A_{q+i} − A_{q+i+1}|, and l.229 holds as printed (noCircuit_step). The run gives the agreement a_{i+k} = a_{i+1+k} on ⟦1, q−1⟧ that the strict three_pow_dvd_Aun_sub needs. 2^{p_n} − 3ⁿ divides every A_u (noCircuit_dvd_Aun) and is prime to 3.

syracuse.tex:227 — « divisible by 3^p » fails for OQ-43's A'. At the cycle of −17, with i = 6 and q = 3 (the run a_7 = a_8 = a_9 = 1), A'_9 − A'_{10} = −2502 = −2·3²·139, and 27 ∤ −2502 (noCircuit_alt_three_pow_false). What holds is 3^{q−1}(2^{p_n} − 3ⁿ) ∣ A'_{q+i} − A'_{q+i+1} (noCircuit_step_alt). This is another conjunct in favour of the printed A_u^n (OQ-43).

syracuse.tex:232–234 — the display is false as printed, in both index readings and both readings of OQ-43. The true identity, for n-periodic a with a_{i+k} = 1 on ⟦1, q⟧ and 1 ≤ q ≤ n, is A_{q+i} − A_{q+i+1} = 3^q Σ_{m=1}^{n−q} 3^{n−q−m} 2^{a_{q+i+1}+⋯+a_{q+i+m−1}} (2 − 2^{a_{q+i+m}}) (noCircuit_diff_eq). For A' it holds with 3(A'_{q+i} − A'_{q+i+1}) on the left (noCircuit_diff_eq_alt). The printed sum stops at n − 1 − p with 3^{n−1−p−k}, so it misses the term m = n − p, which can be nonzero: at −17 with i = 6, p = 3 it is −224 of the total −278. It is not the largest in general: at −17 with i = 3, p = 2 the terms are (−1134, 0, 0, 0, −256), and when the run extends to the left (a_i = 1) the term is 0, since then a_{p+i+(n−p)} = a_i = 1. At −17 (i = 6, p = 3), 3^{−3}(A_9 − A_{10}) = −278 and 3^{−3}(A'_9 − A'_{10}) = −2502/27. The display is −110 with the literal indices and −18 with the summation index restored (noCircuit_display_printed_false). The step 2^{a_{p+i}} = 2 at l.234 is correct (a_{p+i} is the last term of the run).

syracuse.tex:235–236 — the bound is an unproved step. Signed, as printed, the chain bounds a negative number: A_{q+i} − A_{q+i+1} < 0 (noCircuit_upper), so l.235–236 hold trivially. l.229 needs them in absolute value. There, what follows from the identity and a ≥ 1 is 3·2ⁿ |A_{q+i} − A_{q+i+1}| ≤ 2·3ⁿ (2^{p_n} − 2ⁿ), that is 3^{−q}|…| ≤ 2·3^{n−q−1}(2^{p_n−n} − 1) (noCircuit_abs_diff_le). From a ≥ 1 and Σa alone this is sharp (noCircuitSum_bound_sharp), and it is attained at the cycle (−5, −7) (noCircuit_bound_sharp_seq12). l.235 holds under the partial-sum bound 2^{a_{p+i+1}+⋯+a_{p+i+m}} ≤ (3+η)^m, which the stray display l.253 writes (noCircuit_l235_of_eta). That hypothesis holds at −17 with η = 1 (noCircuit_l235_nonvacuous_seq17), but nothing in the draft proves it.

syracuse.tex:236 — the second inequality is false for small η. If 2 log 3 (3^η − 1) < 1, then for all large n and every p ≤ εn, 3^{n−p}(3^{nη} − 1)/(3^η − 1) > 2 log 3 · 3^{(1−ε+η)n} (noCircuit_l236_false). The true form has 1/(3^η − 1) in place of 2 log 3. With the natural log, which the Lean statement uses, the condition is η < 0.341. It is η < 0.652 with log₁₀ (the base the constant of l.241 matches) and η < 0.250 with log₂ (the base l.243 needs). The draft's log is not consistent, so the number depends on the reading, but the failure for small η holds in every base. l.244 needs η < ε, so for ε below the threshold (0.341, 0.652 or 0.250) the printed chain cannot run.

syracuse.tex:239–244 — under the partial-sum bound of l.253, with x > 0, the proof's p ≥ εn, and theo:matveev's shape as a hypothesis, l.244 holds in the form 3^{n(ε−η)}(3^η − 1) < (e p_n)^C (noCircuit_l244_of_eta). The printed form has 2(log(3+η) n)^{3.7·10⁸} on the right, with no factor 3^η − 1. The passage from (e p_n)^C to 3.7·10⁸ is not derived.

syracuse.tex:243 — « p_n ≤ n log(3+η) » is false with the natural logarithm, which the draft uses elsewhere (l.114–124, l.146). On every cycle of x > 0 and for 0 ≤ η ≤ 1, n log(3 + η) < p_n (noCircuit_l243_natural_log_false), since p_n > n log₂ 3. The log of l.243 must be log₂, as in l.253. « 2^{p_n} ≥ 3ⁿ » (l.243) holds only for x > 0 (OQ-63 (a)); the true l.244 does not need it.

syracuse.tex:241 — the constant: ½ e 2^{4.5} 30⁵ log 3 > 7·10⁸ with the natural logarithm, more than the exponent 3.7·10⁸ of l.244. The printed ≃ 3.6·10⁸ is the value with log₁₀ 3, which lies in (3.5·10⁸, 3.6·10⁸) (noCircuit_matveev_constant). theo:matveev has d = 3.5·10⁶ at l.158. Here C is a parameter, so none of these is used.

syracuse.tex:219 — « the known ones » is not defined. Read as the cycle (1, 4, 2) of the abstract (l.42), the statement is false: the fixed point (−1) is an ε-circuit for every ε (strict isCircuit_neg_one; noCircuitStatement_false_of_neg_one, for every K without −1). The cycle (−5, −7) is an ε-circuit for ε ≤ 1 (isCircuit_neg_five) and that of −17 for ε ≤ 4/7 (noCircuit_isCircuit_neg_seventeen; 3/7 in the proof's reading). With the printed p ≥ εn − 1, the statement implies that every cycle of ℤ of period n ≤ 10¹⁴ is a known one (noCircuitStatement_period_le, by p = 0).

syracuse.tex:251–257 — the stray display after the proof is not part of it and is not formalized. Its first line is 0 as printed: the two exponents Σ_{j=0}^{k−1} a_{p+j}(y) coincide. Its left side is nonzero (noCircuit_diff_ne_zero).
syracuse.tex:221–247 — the true identity, the bound, the threshold log₃(3/2) and the finiteness are not in the draft; the proofs here are new.
questions: « the known ones » (l.219, reading (1)). Reading taken: none. The statement is recorded as NoCircuitStatement K with K a parameter, and the reading of the four known cycles of ℤ is noCircuitKnown. Under the reading 'the positive cycle (1, 4, 2)' (l.42), the statement is refuted at (−1).

p ≥ εn − 1 (def:circuit, l.216) or p ≥ εn (the proof, l.222)? (OQ-63 (d), reading (2).) Reading taken: both. The steps hold for every q. The finiteness is proved for the printed, weaker condition, which covers the proof's. NoCircuitStatement uses IsCircuit, the printed one. With it, every cycle with εn ≤ 1 is an ε-circuit.

x (l.222) or y (l.225) (reading (3))? Reading taken: one circuit, with A_u(y) read as A_u(a(x)) and the run at a_{i+k}(x). Read with y = T^i(x), A_{p+i}(a(y)) = A_{p+2i}(a(x)), and the run no longer ends at that index when i ≠ 0, so the 3-adic step would not follow from the run. The reading is equivalent to A_p(a(y)).

η (l.235–244, reading (4)) is never defined. Reading taken: the exponent of the partial-sum bound of l.253, 2^{a_{p+i+1}+⋯+a_{p+i+m}} ≤ (3+η)^m, carried as an explicit hypothesis in the η-forms only. The η-free bound and the threshold log₃(3/2) do not depend on it. The question is whether the author has a proof of such a bound with η < ε. None is in the draft, and l.236 fails for η < 0.341 with the natural log (0.652 with log₁₀, 0.250 with log₂).
Is n meant to be ≥ 2 (l.222)? Reading taken: n ≥ 2. The step is false at n = 1, but the circuits of period 1 are the known fixed points (1) and (−1).

« 2^{p_n} ≥ 3ⁿ » (l.243; OQ-63 (a), reading (5)): positive cycles only? Reading taken: none needed for the true l.244, which holds on every cycle of ℤ from l.240 as printed (NoCircuitMatveevAbs). The η-form in the paper's shape is stated for x > 0, from theo:matveev's shape (NoCircuitMatveev).

Matveev's constant (reading (6)): d = 3.5·10⁶ (l.158), C ≈ 3.6·10⁸ (l.241) or 3.7·10⁸ (l.244)? Reading taken: C is a parameter of the hypothesis, with C ≥ 0 for the finiteness. The printed 3.6·10⁸ matches log₁₀ 3, not log 3 (noCircuit_matveev_constant).
The log of « p_n ≤ n log(3 + η) » (l.243). Reading taken: log₂. With the natural log it is false on every positive cycle. It is not used: p_n ≤ 2n replaces it.
OQ-43: A_u printed or the product to n − 2 − k? Reading taken: both. The 3-adic step as printed (3^p) holds only for the printed A_u^n; for A' it is 3^{p−1}.

kb_proposals: On a cycle of least period n ≥ 2, A_{q+i} − A_{q+i+1} at the end of a run of q ascending indices is 3^q times an explicit sum of nonpositive terms (Syracuse.noCircuit_diff_eq, noCircuitSum). Bound it by induction on the window with one nlinarith step (noCircuitSum_bound). The bound is sharp, and attained at (−5, −7).

A cited inequality with a free constant (Matveev): state it as a Prop with the constant as a parameter (NoCircuitMatveev C, NoCircuitMatveevAbs C). Prove the consequence first from the lower bound at the one pair (P, n) (noCircuit_l244_of_lower), then specialise to each form of the hypothesis.

Exponential beats polynomial with a real exponent C: bound (2en)^C by (2e)^⌈C⌉₊ n^⌈C⌉₊ (Real.rpow_le_rpow_of_exponent_le, base ≥ 1), then use tendsto_pow_const_div_const_pow_of_one_lt (Syracuse.noCircuit_eventually). No hypothesis on the sign of C is needed.

Real.exp_one_gt_d9 and exp_one_lt_d9 need import Mathlib.Analysis.Complex.ExponentialBounds, which Syracuse.TwoDescents does not import. Bound log₁₀ 3 through 10^47 < 3^100 < 10^48, with Real.log_lt_log and Real.log_pow.

From IsCircuit ε x to the step lemmas: isCircuit_iff_minimalPeriod, then α := aPer n x (aPer_natCast) and the run at i = m via a_iterate. Function.not_isPeriodicPt_of_pos_of_lt_minimalPeriod takes n ≠ 0, not 0 < n (noCircuit_period_bounded_of).

An existential bound in front of an implication is a tautology: ∃ B, (∀ x, P x → f x ≤ B → Q x) → ∀ x, P x → Q x holds for every P, Q (take B = f of a counterexample). State the bound as a conjunct, ∃ B, (∀ x, P x → f x ≤ B) ∧ …, or quantify B before the reading (T-syr-no-circuit AUDIT-1, noCircuit_of_cited).
notes: One new file, scaffold/SyracuseScaffold/NoCircuit.lean (0 sorry, no warning under -DwarningAsError=true). It imports Syracuse.TwoDescents and Mathlib.Analysis.Complex.ExponentialBounds, the latter for the bounds on exp 1. It is not added to the scaffold root, as dispatched. `lake build SyracuseScaffold.NoCircuit` ran once at the end and succeeded; only that module was built. #print axioms of the principal declarations gives propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound only. Every name has the prefix noCircuit / NoCircuit, and none clashes with the strict Syracuse.* (checked by grep). No mark: the row stays partial. It waits on T-syr-cited (the Matveev hypothesis), OQ-63 and the unfinished conclusion. The statement is a Prop (NoCircuitStatement K), not a sorry'd theorem, so the file can graduate to the strict tree as is. The cited input is a hypothesis in each statement that uses it: NoCircuitMatveev C or NoCircuitMatveevAbs C. T-syr-cited-steps may carry its own Matveev Prop in CitedSteps.lean, which I did not read. If both graduate, the master may want one of the two forms, but they need not be unified. Non-vacuity: the step and the bound are instantiated at (−5, −7) and at the cycle of −17. The x > 0 forms (noCircuit_l244_pos, noCircuit_period_bounded_pos, noCircuit_l244_of_eta) have no known instance with n ≥ 2: their hypotheses describe a hypothetical non-trivial positive cycle, the object of the statement. Fix round 1 (AUDIT-1, major). noCircuit_of_cited is restated with the bound as its first conjunct, B fixed before K. Its earlier form was a tautology, and its docstring now says so, so that nobody reintroduces it. SCOPE and findings[0] no longer present it as content beyond noCircuit_period_bounded. Minor fixes: finding 3 no longer says the missing term is the largest; the l.236 threshold is given in all three log bases; the non-vacuity lemmas include the periodicity of seq17 and seq12; and the wording is now « the four known cycles of ℤ ».
